questions.question: What's the simplest way to decide whether an integration is inbound or outbound?
options: Check which direction the data ends up flowing
Ask 'who dials the phone?' — whichever system starts the conversation
Inbound always uses REST, outbound always uses SOAP
It depends on which system stores the data permanently
questions.explanation: Direction is about who initiates the call, not which way data ends up moving — 'who dials the phone?' is the shortcut for remembering this.

questions.question: A mobile app calls the Salesforce REST API to read and update Account records. From Salesforce's point of view, is this inbound or outbound?
options: Outbound, because Salesforce is sending Account data back
Inbound, because the mobile app started the conversation
Neither — REST API calls don't have a direction
It depends on whether the app is reading or writing
questions.explanation: The mobile app calls Salesforce first, so this is inbound — regardless of whether the response sends data back out.

questions.question: Which of these is a typical outbound integration tool?
options: A custom Apex REST endpoint exposed for another system to call
An Apex callout using HttpRequest and HttpResponse
The Bulk API used by an external system to load records
The Pub/Sub API used by another system to subscribe to events
questions.explanation: An Apex callout is Salesforce initiating the conversation — that's outbound. The other three options all involve another system calling into Salesforce.

questions.question: Why is it incorrect to say 'inbound integrations are always more secure than outbound ones'?
options: Because outbound integrations never need authentication
Because both directions need their own authentication, and either can be set up carelessly
Because inbound integrations don't use HTTP
Because Salesforce only allows outbound integrations to be secured
questions.explanation: Security depends on how each direction is configured, not on direction itself — a carelessly secured inbound endpoint is no safer than a carelessly secured outbound callout.

questions.question: A payment gateway calls a Salesforce endpoint to confirm a payment succeeded. What kind of integration is this?
options: Outbound, because Salesforce receives the confirmation
Inbound, because the payment gateway started the call
Batch, because it only happens once per payment
Neither, because webhooks don't count as integrations
questions.explanation: The payment gateway dials the phone, so this is inbound — a classic webhook pattern.
